questions: Are the involuntary movements sudden, brief jerks rather than a rhythmic tremor?
Do the movements predominantly involve the neck and shoulders?
Did these movements worsen after zonisamide was discontinued?
Do you have a history of epilepsy or epileptic seizures?
Are the movements absent during sleep?
Are the abnormal movements sustained twisting or posturing of the hands or arms?
Can you voluntarily suppress the movements for several seconds?
Do you feel an inner urge or mounting discomfort before performing the movement?
Do the movements lessen or disappear when you are distracted or performing a different mental task?
Did the movements begin after starting any medication other than zonisamide?
Are the abnormal movements sustained twisting or posturing of the hands or arms?
Can you voluntarily suppress the movements for several seconds?
Do you feel an inner urge or mounting discomfort before performing the movement?
Do the movements lessen or disappear when you are distracted or performing a different mental task?
Did the movements begin after starting any medication other than zonisamide?
Do your hands or arms shake rhythmically when you hold them outstretched?
Is the shaking worse when you use your hands for a precise action, such as writing or drinking?
Is the shaking present when your arms are completely relaxed at rest?
Did the abnormal movements improve after zonisamide was restarted?
Have you noticed slowness, stiffness, balance problems, or reduced facial expression?
Did the rigidity and postural instability begin while you were taking zonisamide?
Did the rigidity and postural instability improve after zonisamide was stopped?
Have you ever taken an antipsychotic, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, or other dopamine-blocking medication?
Did the symptoms begin suddenly over days or weeks rather than gradually over months or years?
Is the postural tremor markedly reduced when you are distracted or when you perform a task with the other hand?
Is the tremor irregular or jerky rather than a smooth, regular oscillation?
Does the tremor change in frequency or direction when you shift your arms into different positions?
Is there a marked difference in tremor severity between the two arms?
Do you have difficulty with coordination, such as reaching accurately or performing rapid alternating hand movements?
Have you developed difficulty with speech, swallowing, eye movements, or autonomic symptoms such as fainting or urinary problems?
Did the tremor start in one arm before appearing in the other?
Is the more affected arm also the side with greater rigidity?
Do you have a family history of tremor or Parkinson-like symptoms?
Did the tremor begin before the stiffness and postural instability?
Have you had a stroke, head injury, brain tumor, or other structural brain disorder?
orders: A focused movement-disorder examination assessing bradykinesia, rigidity, gait, postural stability, facial expression, and rest, postural, and re-emergent tremor.
A dopamine-transporter SPECT (DaTscan) to evaluate presynaptic nigrostriatal dopaminergic deficit.
A standardized levodopa challenge with carbidopa/levodopa, assessing rigidity, postural instability, and postural tremor before and after the dose.
